summary: Preserved PR 3167's valid ordinary-TP entry-rank-only grammar compilation, masking, and token broadcast. Independently reproduced both PR 3202 counterexamples against the candidate implementation: speculative TP and active context-parallel TP select the legacy path, so a simulated non-entry rank submits its own grammar lookup. No further source correction is justified on the assigned one-GPU architecture because speculative verification requires synchronized per-rank FSM/tree state and context parallelism requires ownership and collectives across orthogonal attention CP and TP groups.

tests.what_was_measured: Candidate source behavior on a simulated non-entry rank: speculative-TP and CP-active-TP each made one grammar backend lookup and received a Future; ordinary TP made zero and installed PlaceholderGrammarObject.

Preserved candidate compatibility/regression suite: 97 passed, including ordinary-TP compile-once behavior, failure synchronization, broadcast selection, legacy fallback, and no collective for unconstrained batches.
All retained changed Python modules compile successfully.

tests.command: inline torch ROCm masked-argmax reference (output in reports/j-3d84fe484c6b/raw/gpu-reference.txt)
tests.what_was_measured: On the assigned AMD Instinct MI350X, masked argmax [2, 1] matched the independent allowed-token reference [2, 1]. This measures mask numerics only, not distributed serving.

gpu_execution.evidence: Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 executed the numerical mask reference on one AMD Instinct MI350X. torch.cuda.device_count() returned 1, so TP/CP distributed serving was not executed.

remaining_limitations: Speculative TP still compiles and applies grammar state per rank; a safe change must synchronize verify-tree masks, FSM advancement, accept lengths, accept indexes, and committed output tokens.

Active context-parallel TP still compiles and applies grammar state in every applicable attention-TP group; a safe change needs ownership and collectives spanning the orthogonal attention CP and TP request topology.
Only one GPU was assigned, so true speculative TP, context-parallel TP, distributed serving, and end-to-end overhead measurement remain unverified.
The deterministic tiny Llama fixture validates transport and engine execution only and cannot qualify the missing distributed architectures; it was not used as substitute evidence.
No native sources changed, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
